helpToggle.title: Show or hide help labels on every button

btn-freehand.brief: Freehand mode: draw on top of Ketcher with a pen, finger, trackpad or mouse.
btn-freehand.student: Turn this on and draw the mechanism as on paper: bonds as lines (zig-zag chains and rings can be one stroke), atom labels as letters, charges as + or −, and curved arrows with a head. The pen bar below sets colour, line and input. Turn it off to use Ketcher's own tools again.

btn-recognize.brief: Recognize the ink and propose a clean structure.
btn-recognize.student: MecHand reads your strokes in the browser (no server), shows what it understood and checks the electron flow of the curved arrows. Confirm to insert it into Ketcher.

btn-undo-ink.brief: Undo the last change to the ink (stroke, erasure or clear).
btn-undo-ink.student: Undoes the last stroke, erasure or clear. Ketcher's structure is not touched.

btn-redo-ink.student: Puts back the last change that Undo ink removed.

btn-clear-ink.student: Deletes all freehand strokes that have not been inserted yet. Undo ink brings them back.

tool-pen.student: The pen draws strokes. Choose its colour, kind of line and width on this bar.

tool-eraser.brief: Erase whole strokes by touching them.
tool-eraser.student: Drag over the strokes you want to remove (they fade) and lift: they are erased. The eraser end of a pen (Surface, Wacom) erases too, whatever tool is selected.

pen-colour.student: Colours help you organise a drawing (e.g. arrows in red). Recognition ignores colour.

pen-style.brief: Kind of line: ballpoint, fountain pen, marker or dashed.
pen-style.student: Ballpoint draws an even line; the fountain pen follows pen pressure (or speed with a mouse); the marker is broad and translucent; dashed is only a look. All are recognized the same way.

pen-width.student: From fine to extra bold. Only the look changes; recognition uses the shape of the stroke.

pen-input.brief: Which inputs draw: auto, pen only, pen and finger, or trackpad.
pen-input.student: Auto: once you use a pen, fingers and palms are ignored. Pen only: fingers never draw. Pen and finger: both draw. Trackpad: click to start a stroke, move without pressing, click to end it (no click-and-drag needed).

pen-device.brief: The device of the last contact, and whether it could draw.
pen-device.student: Shows whether the browser saw a pen, a finger or a mouse/trackpad. "Ignored" means palm rejection discarded the contact; change the input mode if your finger should draw.

btn-library.brief: Template library; also draws a molecule from its SMILES, InChI, CAS number or name.
btn-library.student: Rings, functional groups, biomolecules, reagents and complete mechanisms. Search by name, formula or CAS number, or type a SMILES or InChI to draw it. Names that are not in the library can be looked up online (PubChem, OPSIN) if you ask.

btn-export.brief: Export to TikZ, chemfig, ChemDraw (CDXML), MOL/RXN, KET or SMILES.
btn-export.student: Converts the Ketcher canvas, including curved arrows, into code for your LaTeX document, or into files that ChemDraw, Marvin and other editors open.

btn-teach.student: Draw a few examples of a letter or sign, an arrow, a bond or a lone pair. They are stored in this browser and used immediately; export them to contribute them to the shared model.

btn-about.brief: Version, recognition model and browser support.
btn-about.student: Shows the version, the recognition model in use, what it can read, and known browser issues.

btn-help.brief: Help centre: topics, tips for what you are doing, a guided tour and shortcuts.
btn-help.student: Opens the help centre on the topic of what you are doing now. You can search it, replay the guided tour or see all the keyboard shortcuts.

btn-language.student: Choose the language of MecHand's buttons, dialogs and help. Translations are plain JSON files that anyone can add or improve.

btn-help-toggle.brief: Show or hide these help labels.
btn-help-toggle.student: Toggle the help labels. Choose Expert for one-liners or Student for explanations.

btn-periodic.brief: Simple periodic table: valence electrons, usual bonds, lone pairs and electronegativity.
btn-periodic.student: Opens a simple periodic table beside the canvas. Click an element to see how many valence electrons, bonds and lone pairs it usually has, and how electronegative it is; you can also pick it to draw it in Ketcher.

btn-level.brief: User level: A student, B advanced student, C researcher.
btn-level.student: Your level changes what MecHand offers: A (secondary school, first years) has basic templates and chemistry explanations; B (end of degree, master's, start of PhD) the whole library; C (research) everything.

btn-image.brief: Read a mechanism from an image: a photo of a drawing on paper, a scan, or a figure from an article or book.
btn-image.student: Choose, drop or paste (Ctrl/⌘+V) an image. MecHand reads it in this browser — bonds, labels, charges, wedges, curved and straight arrows — shows what it read, and inserts it into Ketcher or loads it as ink to correct with the pen and eraser.

about.title: About MecHand recognition
about.intro: MecHand reads your **strokes** (not a picture of them) directly in the browser: no installation, no server, nothing leaves your computer. Lines become bonds (chains and rings can be one stroke), parallel lines become double/triple bonds, letters become atom labels, + and − become charges, and curved strokes with a head become electron-flow arrows (full head = 2 e⁻, single barb = 1 e⁻). Each arrow is anchored to the nearest atom or bond and checked for electron bookkeeping.
about.engineLocked: In-browser only (study mode: nothing leaves this browser).
about.engineLevel: In-browser recognition only. The optional recognition server is offered at level C (Researcher).
about.engineServer: DECIMER server (optional, image-based, runs on your computer; arrows and charges still come from the in-browser recognizer)
about.browsersText: Works in current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari (desktop and iPad). Known differences are listed in the guide under “Browser support”.

teach.title: 1. Training (about 10 minutes)
teach.intro: Teach MecHand your handwriting. Open **✍ Teach** and save about 3 samples of each:
teach.letters: *{tab}*: C, O, N, H, F, l (of Cl), r (of Br), a (of Na), +, − (and ⊕, ⊖ if you write them circled)
teach.arrows: *{tab}*: curved 2 e⁻ arrow, reaction arrow, equilibrium
teach.reading: Under the box you will see how MecHand reads it. If it gets it right (✓), there is no need to insist.

task.ketcherTip: Curved arrows in Ketcher: arrow tool → “Arrow Elliptical Arc Open Angle” (2 e⁻) or “… Open Half Angle” (1 e⁻). Charges: the “A+” and “A−” tools.
task.confirmSkip: Do you want to skip this task?

condition.freehand: MecHand: freehand drawing (you can correct with Ketcher's tools)

stimulus.practica-acid-base: Practice (does not count): draw the whole reaction, with both curved arrows, the reaction arrow and the products. Try out the tools you will need.
stimulus.A3-sn2-walden: Draw the reactants with the curved arrows and the organic product. You do not need to draw the transition state (in brackets), the stereochemistry (wedges), the Na⁺ or the NaBr.
stimulus.A4-aldol-basic: Draw only the first step (top left): the aldehyde and the hydroxide ion with the three curved arrows, the equilibrium arrow and the enolate that forms. Where there is an R, put a CH₃ (the end of a line is enough).
stimulus.B3-sn2-cianur: Draw the reactants with the curved arrows and the organic product. You do not need to draw the lone pairs, the Na⁺ or the Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions of the products.
stimulus.B4-aldol-acid: Draw only the second step (top, the second and third compounds): the protonated aldehyde and water with the three curved arrows, the equilibrium arrow and the enol that forms. Where there is an R, put a CH₃ (the end of a line is enough).

start.title: Getting started
body: MecHand adds hand drawing to the Ketcher chemical editor. Everything runs in your browser.
1. Press **Freehand** and draw the molecule or mechanism as on paper.
2. Press **Recognize** (Space): MecHand shows what it read and checks the curved arrows.
3. **Insert into Ketcher**, then edit with Ketcher's tools, or **Export** to LaTeX, ChemDraw or Marvin.
The **Library** (Ctrl/⌘+K) gives you ready-made structures and complete mechanisms, and draws any molecule from its SMILES, InChI, CAS number or name.

drawing.title: How to draw
body: **Bonds**: straight lines. A zig-zag or a closed polygon can be one stroke; two or three close parallel lines are a double or triple bond.
**Atoms**: write the letters (C, H, N, O, S, P, F, Cl, Br, I, Na…) at the end of a bond, leaving a small gap.
**Charges**: + or − (also ⊕, ⊖, 2−) up and to the right of the atom. **Lone pairs and radicals**: two dots or one dot next to the atom.
**Curved arrows**: start at the electrons (a lone pair or the middle of a bond) and end at the atom or bond that receives them. A full head (V) moves two electrons, a single barb one.
**Reactions**: a long straight arrow between reactants and products, and + between molecules.
Draw bonds two or three times longer than letters are tall: that is how MecHand tells them apart.

penbar.title: The pen bar
body: In freehand mode, a second toolbar sets the **pen** or the **eraser** (P / E). The eraser removes whole strokes; the eraser end of a Surface or Wacom pen erases too.
**Colour, kind of line and width** only change the look of the ink; recognition uses the shape of the strokes.
**Input mode**: *Auto* ignores fingers and palms once a pen has been used; *Pen only* never lets a finger draw; *Pen and finger* lets both draw; *Trackpad* draws by click – move – click.
The **device chip** shows whether the browser saw a pen, a finger or a mouse/trackpad, and whether the contact was ignored.

recognize.title: Recognition and corrections
body: **Recognize** colours your ink by how it was read: blue bonds, green labels, red arrows, grey not understood.
If something is misread: **Keep drawing** (Esc), erase the stroke (E) and draw it again, larger and with clearer gaps between bonds and letters.
The **electron-flow check** warns when an arrow starts at an atom without a lone pair, starts or ends on nothing, or gives C, N, O or F more than an octet.
After inserting, Ketcher's tools fix anything else (atom type, charge, bond order).
If the same symbol is misread again and again, teach it to MecHand (**Teach**).

library.title: Template library and structures from text
body: Open it with **Library** or Ctrl/⌘+K and type: names in English, Catalan or Spanish, abbreviations (Trp, THF), formulas, CAS numbers. Accents and small typos do not matter.
Enter adds the highlighted structure next to your drawing; mechanisms replace the canvas. Shift+Enter does the opposite. Ctrl/⌘+D keeps a favourite.
Type a **SMILES** or an **InChI** and it is drawn at once, offline.
For other **names or CAS numbers**, press **Look up online** (Alt+Enter): only the text you typed is sent to PubChem (and OPSIN).

teach.title: Teach MecHand your handwriting
body: **Teach** stores examples of your own handwriting in this browser and uses them at once.
*Letters & signs*: a few samples of each symbol MecHand misreads. *Arrows*: arrowheads drawn as a separate stroke teach your style of head. *Electrons*: the size of your dots.
**Export samples** saves them as a file that can be added to the shared model.

export.title: Export
body: **Export** converts the whole canvas: **TikZ** (curved arrows as Bézier curves) and **chemfig** for LaTeX, **CDXML** for ChemDraw, **MOL/RXN** for Marvin and RDKit, **KET** and **SMILES**.
Copy the code, or download it as a file.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
body: `Alt+F` Freehand on/off · `Space` Recognize · `P` / `E` pen / eraser
`Ctrl/⌘+Z` undo ink · `Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Z` redo ink · `Esc` drop an open trackpad stroke, close a dialog
`Ctrl/⌘+K` library · `F1` this help
In the library: arrows move, `Enter` inserts, `Shift+Enter` the other way, `Ctrl/⌘+D` favourite, `Alt+Enter` look up online.
In the recognition dialog: `Enter` inserts, `Esc` keeps drawing. With Freehand off, Ketcher's own shortcuts work.

privacy.title: Privacy
body: Your drawings and handwriting samples never leave your browser: there is no server.
Settings, Teach samples and favourites are kept in this browser's storage only.
The only network use after loading is the optional online look-up of a name in the library, and only when you ask for it.

translate.title: Translations
body: MecHand's interface is translated with one plain JSON file per language. To add or improve a language, copy `en.json` from `src/i18n/locales/`, translate the texts and send it to the project (a pull request or an e-mail).
Missing texts appear in English, so a partial translation already works. Ketcher's own toolbars are not translated by MecHand.

levels.title: Levels: student, advanced, researcher
body: MecHand adapts to who uses it. Choose your level in the **Level** menu of the bar:
**A · Student** (secondary school and first years of a degree): basic templates, the simple periodic table and an explanation of every arrow you draw.
**B · Advanced student** (end of a degree, master's, start of a PhD): the whole template library and online look-up of names and CAS numbers.
**C · Researcher**: everything, including the optional recognition server. Levels B and C can turn the chemistry explanations of level A on in this help.
A teacher can share a link with `?level=A` (or B, C) at the end of the address: MecHand then opens at that level.
